query: How do review themes differ between positive and negative IMDb sentiment?

per_column.name: primary_critique_focus
per_column.rationale: Categorizes which aspect of a film the review centers on (plot, acting, screenplay, etc.). Well-separated, interpretable categories that can be cross-tabulated against sentiment to reveal which themes dominate positive vs negative reviews. Directly serves the query about theme differences.

per_column.name: narrative_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Interpretable ordinal-ish categories (coherent/engaging vs convoluted/thin vs derivative) that are associational to sentiment without being a bare restatement of the label. Enables meaningful segmentation, though it correlates strongly with sentiment; still informative as a theme dimension.

per_column.name: comparison_or_genre_context
per_column.rationale: External rhetorical dimension (whether reviewer compares to other films, contextualizes by genre, or references history/culture). Clean, well-separated categories orthogonal to the label, offering a genuinely exploratory relationship to compare against sentiment.

per_column.name: technical_or_creative_root_cause
per_column.rationale: Attributes the review's judgment to a source (writing, casting, direction, effects, budget). Interpretable, well-spread categories that support discovering which root causes align with positive vs negative sentiment. Strong EDA variable.

per_column.name: recommendation_stance
per_column.rationale: Captures explicit/implicit recommend/avoid stance. Interpretable and segmentable, but it is largely a near-proxy for sentiment polarity, so it partially restates the focus rather than opening an independent relationship; still usable for segmentation.

judge.rationale: As a set, these columns provide interpretable, well-separated categorical dimensions (critique focus, narrative quality, comparative context, root-cause attribution, recommendation stance) that can each be grouped and cross-tabulated against label_pos to explore how review themes differ by sentiment. Categories are human-readable and reasonably balanced rather than opaque scores or near-constant/fine-grained values. The main caveats are that narrative_quality_signal and recommendation_stance correlate very tightly with sentiment and thus partly restate the focus, but the remaining columns (especially primary_critique_focus, comparison_or_genre_context, and technical_or_creative_root_cause) supply genuinely orthogonal, thematically rich segmentation. Overall a strong realization of the exploratory-EDA claim.
